standard_prerequisites: Formally smooth morphism of rings: the lifting property against square-zero ideal extensions, namely every solid commutative diagram into R and R/I with I squared zero admits a dotted lift making the diagram commute

The group algebra k of the additive group of the rationals: the k-algebra with basis x-alpha indexed by rational alpha and multiplication x-alpha x-beta equals x of alpha plus beta, so x-zero is the unit
For a surjective ring map with kernel J, the obstruction to lifting against a square-zero extension A-prime to A with kernel I is the induced map J over J squared into I
A nonzerodivisor mapping to zero shows a ring map is not flat
core_obligations: Let k be a field of positive characteristic p and let A be the group algebra k[Q] with augmentation map to k sending every basis element x-alpha to one; the kernel J is generated by the elements x-alpha minus one

In J over J squared the classes z-alpha of x-alpha minus one satisfy z of alpha plus beta equals z-alpha plus z-beta, and in characteristic p the binomial-type identity p times z of alpha over p equals zero forces z-alpha equals zero for every alpha; hence J over J squared is zero

Given a solid diagram from k of Q to k and to A-prime over a square-zero extension A-prime to A, the obstruction to lifting the augmentation is the induced map from J over J squared into the kernel I; since J over J squared is zero the obstruction vanishes and the lift exists, so the augmentation is formally smooth
The map is not flat: the element x-two minus one is a nonzerodivisor in k of Q whose image in k is zero

Hence there exists a formally smooth ring map which is not flat; by contrast, in characteristic zero the computation J over J squared equals Q tensor over Z k shows the obstruction is nonzero, so the augmentation is not formally smooth in that case
proof_roadmap: Compute J over J squared for the group algebra augmentation via the additive relation
Derive the vanishing in positive characteristic and conclude formal smoothness
Exhibit the nonzerodivisor dying in the target to break flatness
